thread:
elaine: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I see steady memory growth on several longcontext workloads. Not full OOM, but resident set keeps creeping and fragmentation looks worse. Any ideas? :eyes:
ben: saw similar on the perf cluster. Latency fine but RSS +24% over 8h on a 1k-token stream test.
raghu: can you paste pmap/memstat or the runtime heap dump?
elaine: quick dump attached below (trimmed):
```
RSS: 15.2G
heap: 10.7G
cache_alloc: 6.1G
free_frag_blocks: 1.9G
bucket_64: 4.9% used
bucket_256: 71.3% used
long_lived_kv: 28.5% of entries
```

elaine: noticing a lot of small gaps between KV blocks — allocator is preferring 256B granularity after kernel change, even when we only need ~70-120 bytes for KV entries. That means internal fragmentation + more pages pinned.
sasha: hmm, kernel selector bump to v2.7 changed the preferred kernel tiling for attention, maybe it also changed allocator hints (we passed different alignment to the runtime). Could be alignment/alignment-quantization interplay.
zoe: i ran a micro repro where we keep appending longcontexts: after 2k requests fragmentation ratio hits 0.22 and RSS plateaus at a higher baseline. I'll drop the script in the repo.
ben: quick ask — is this purely allocator fragmentation or are pages being swapped to host/paged out?
perf-bot: perf report (short):
```
- hot paths: kv_insert (28%), kv_lookup (17%), kv_compact_background (3%)
- syscalls increased: madvise MADV_DONTNEED calls decreased by 60%
- page faults: minor PF up 12%, major PF unchanged
```

raghu: decreased MADV_DONTNEED sounds like we're not releasing freed blocks back to the OS, which aligns with internal fragmentation. The allocator coalescer maybe failing because adjacent free blocks are in different buckets now.
elaine: idea: introduce a short "reuse window" where recently freed small blocks are preferentially reused for similar-size KV entries for first N seconds instead of going to large buckets. That reduces scattering. Thoughts?
sasha: +1, but we have to be careful about long-lived entries: reusing for short-lived entries could increase churn. Need metrics: lifetime hist by bucket.
zoe: i can add histogram instrumentation per-bucket with ttl sampling. Cheap to add.

ben: alternative: lower the internal bucket step from 256 -> 128 for sizes <= 512. That reduces internal waste but may increase allocator metadata. We should simulate memory/time tradeoff.
raghu: also consider cooperative background compact: when fragmentation ratio > threshold, spawn a low-priority compactor that performs in-place coalescing and moves cold KV to a shadow region that can be page-aligned. This is heavier but only fires rarely.
elaine: agree on both strategies (reuse window + adjustable bucket step) as short + medium term. For long term we might want a per-workload tuning profile that picks bucket curve based on observed size/lifetime dist.
perf-bot: regression check: after reverting kernel-selector to v2.6 on canary, RSS returned to baseline on one test run. Suggests new kernel influenced allocation patterns.
zoe: i'll run the hist sampler and reuse-window microbench tomorrow and post numbers.

sasha: for the reuse window: propose API like set_reuse_window_ms(2000) default 0 in hosted. We can expose disabled in Dedicated because some customers prefer deterministic reuse.
raghu: compaction triggers: frag_ratio > 0.18 && free_frag_blocks > 1GB && low_cpu_window(5m) => schedule compaction. Use staggered backoff to avoid thundering.
ben: we should also add a telemetry counter for "reuse_hits" and "reuse_misses" and track per-bucket. That'll help tune the window.
elaine: action items:
- zoe: add per-bucket size+ttl histogram + basic reuse-window PoC (today)
- ben: add telemetry counters and dashboard for reuse/fragmentation (tomorrow)
- raghu: sketch compactor heuristics + safety constraints (low-priority, snapshot consistency) (EOD)
- sasha: validate whether kernel-selector pass is sending different alignment hints to the allocator (need a small reproducer) (today)

zoe: noted. i'll also run canary with kernel v2.6 vs v2.7 to collect diff traces.

elaine: if PoC looks good, i'll open an RFC PR with microbench numbers and a suggested rollout (feature flag gated). Aim to land reuse-window in staging before next deploy.

ben: one more note — watch out for lock contention: reuse pools may need per-thread caches to avoid global lock storms. Add bench for concurrency.

perf-bot: added ticket perf/kv-frag-330800 in tracker.

elaine: thanks all. keeping this thread as the single place for updates. ping me if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
